evidence.quote: That the valley itself, is like up where you are right now, just coming down from the mountain, is, is pretty barren. It's it's sort of dirt and dust mostly, but along the river valley there's um, you know trees growing, there's you know clusters of, of these vines. And the river itself, although it... So there's a waterfall that comes down off the mountains and cascades down into this pool. And that actually, in the morning light, is, you know the sun is catching it, looks quite pretty, this cascading silvery waterfall. It being or, you know middle spring, the winter rains and snow melt from the top of the mountain have swelled the, the flow of the water. And so you get this you know beautiful cascading—from the water coming off the mountain seems to be clear and pure as it cascades down into this pool.

markers.note: Seeing the pool during the approach does not establish that the party enters or drinks from it.

markers.reading: Walks onto the center of the bridge to use Stone Sense.

evidence.quote: I stroll up onto the bridge and stand in the center of the bridge.
Oh, and I'll do Stone Sense.
If there's anything interesting directly beneath us in the earth. And also, if there's anything interesting in the structure of the bridge.

markers.reading: Return to the castle to free the animals in the stables.

evidence.quote: So um you head back up to the to the castle to free the animals. Seeker, what do you want to do?
Seeker, I'm gonna come over I'm coming over with you and sort of watching and looking at you with the animals.

markers.reading: Rides a lion with the freed animals down the valley as they disperse, then rejoins the group before leading it into the dwarven caves.

evidence.quote: So once, once we get them free, turn to you, Seeker, and say, "I'm going to go down with them and make sure that they get out okay." And I'll climb on the back of one of the lions and ride off with them.
That, that's what seems to happen when you watch Wellby: that he stands there looking at the lion for a moment, and then the lion stops and looks at him.

So the rest of you stand and watch as this procession of, of animals with halfling riding a lion—and it's a very tame lion that seems to be moving with—behaving quite oddly for a lion, like almost like a sheep dog would, right? Like, you know, pacing up and down the sides of this, of this herd of predators, like roaring at them, sort of moving to sort of keep them in line and, and direct, you know, direct the, the, the group away from you and down through the valley. Wellby riding on its back this entire time as they move down the river and out into the valley and begin to disperse.
Wellby leads you here and then down the corridor.

markers.mode: ride a lion, then return on an unstated route

route.reading: Accompanies the predator procession down the river through the valley until it begins dispersing.
Returns to the party, then leads the approach through the dwarven caves.

markers.note: His return is implicit in the later accepted narration placing him back with the party; the exact reunion point is unstated. The proposed dawn-tomorrow instruction does not delay the narrated departure.

markers.reading: Return into the dwarven caves and approach the damaged guardian via the partly barricaded side passage.

evidence.quote: Yes, that's right. Ah, you head back into the dwarven caves and approach the—so, so Wellby had described this, right? There was a sort of—in these caves where Inakara, the, the crazy dwarf person, dwarf-like person, lead you—there was a sort of a side passage that was partially blocked off, like barricaded, like the hobgoblins had—had this is as far as they've gotten and built a sort of defensive position here. And Wellby leads you here and then down the corridor.

route.reading: Take the passage beneath the market area toward the mines and forge.

markers.note: The intervening route from the castle back into the outpost is compressed; this does not establish a surface crossing of the bridge.

markers.reading: Approach the stone guardian while companions hold back.

evidence.quote: I'm definitely going to approach it.

Okay, um, as it, as it begins to—its—so it seems to be not like fully functioning properly, like, as it—as you begin to approach it sort of turns, turns, notices you and start to try to walk forward and begins to try to lift up it's, its axe, but it can't get—it's can't get his arms above, like, you know, it's shoulders. So it's like keeps going like this and sort of trying to, to struggle towards you. And then it, it pauses for a moment. And says, “Stop,” in Dwarven.

markers.note: Seeker accompanies Riswynn; Delwath and Wellby explicitly stay back. No ordered combat begins.

markers.reading: After Riswynn presents the clan shield, pass the guardian into the ruined mineshaft entrance.

evidence.quote: I’ll hold up the shield of the Brawnanvils and say, you know, “My family have been part of this community for generations.”

When it sees the shield, it again—it's like eyes sort of slightly whir and points toward, you know, look towards you, and it, it says now more confidently in Dwarven. And it's voice when it speaks, it sounds, it sounds like stone sort of grating on stone. And it says, 'Yes, my dwarves,' and steps aside.

But there's just giant cracks in the floor going down.

Adamantine.
And that's super valuable. So we should chuck that onto the disk.
Yes.

How deep is this hole?

You come out through the clear water of the mountain stream protecting the back entrance to the dwarven hold, to your horses, the camp you had set up, your giant barrel of oil to burn down the, the plants, you know your, your tents, your you know all the equipment you hadn't bothered to lug with you through the you know, through the mountains.
